You extract one table from a UK public-sector document into JSON.
Return ONLY a JSON object {"rows": [...]} with one object per row of the table, in document order, using exactly these keys:
- date (date): printed as "Date"
- reference (id): printed as "Ref"
- details (text): printed as "Details"
- debit_gbp (money): printed as "Debit"
- credit_gbp (money): printed as "Credit"
- balance_gbp (money): printed as "Balance"
Dates as ISO YYYY-MM-DD. Money as a plain number: no symbols or thousands separators, negative when printed in brackets or with a minus sign. A blank cell is null. Text exactly as printed.
Return every data row of the table and nothing else. Header rows (including a header repeated on a new page), running page headers and footers, totals and subtotals, and the carried-forward and brought-forward lines printed at a page break are not data rows; the opening balance line at the start of a statement is a row. A cell's text can wrap over several lines or continue onto the next page: it is still one cell. When a value such as a date or a name is printed once for a group of rows, or as a heading above the group, it applies to every row of the group, including rows on the next page.
